hero_subtitle: Morocco's pottery capital — Portuguese sea castle, living medina and Atlantic coast.

info.best_time_val: Apr–Jun & Sep–Oct; summer for the beach

overview.title: Welcome to Safi — Portuguese citadel and Atlantic shores
overview.p1: Safi (Asfi), on Morocco's Atlantic coast between El Jadida and Essaouira, is the kingdom's pottery capital. Its Portuguese sea castle, medina, National Ceramics Museum and potters' quarter make it an authentic stop away from the major tourist circuits.
overview.p2: Beyond the walls: the National Ceramics Museum, the potters' quarter, the fishing port and Cap Beddouza. Town life is calm and authentic.
overview.p3: Three to five days work well if you mix water time with the citadel, port and a lalla-fatna afternoon. Summer is lively; winter is milder and still excellent for sports.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Safi
places.subtitle: citadel, dunes, island, pottery and the sea castle.

sea_castle.title: Sea Castle
sea_castle.desc: Underground vaulted hall with columns reflected in water — the city's jewel.

medina.title: Safi Medina
medina.desc: Wall circuit facing the ocean, Angel and Holy Spirit fortifications, period cannons.

ceramics.title: National Ceramics Museum
ceramics.desc: Rare Manueline church still standing inside the citadel.

potters.title: Potters' Quarter
potters.desc: Kilns, workshops and artisans that made Safi's name.

harbor.title: Fishing Port
harbor.desc: Blue boats, daily fish landing and quay activity.

kechla.title: Kechla
kechla.desc: Citadel and panoramas over the old town and ocean.

lalla_fatna.title: Lalla Fatna Beach
lalla_fatna.desc: Long stretch of sand and lively promenade at the foot of the medina.

cap_beddouza.title: Cap Beddouza
cap_beddouza.desc: Large dune-backed beach to the north, often quieter.

souks.title: Souks & Central Market
souks.desc: Spices, fresh fish and crafts in the commercial heart of the city.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2-day itinerary in Safi
itinerary.subtitle: Heritage and pottery first, then coast and relaxation.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Visit the sea castle and walk the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: National Ceramics Museum then potters' workshops.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Fishing port atmosphere and dinner by the sea.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Citadel and panoramas over town and ocean.
detailed_itinerary.day2_a: Afternoon — Lalla Fatna or Cap Beddouza
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Beach or wild headland as you prefer.

eat.title: Where to eat in Safi
eat.subtitle: Grilled fish, seafood and local tables

chez_hosni.title: Restaurant Chez Hosni
chez_hosni.desc: Popular local table praised for generous fish and seafood tagines and friendly service.

chez_said.title: Restaurant Chez Said
chez_said.desc: Well-reviewed seafood and grill spot known for fresh catches and a welcoming host.

riad_du_pecheur.title: Riad du Pêcheur Safi
riad_du_pecheur.desc: Renowned seafood address in Safi combining coastal dishes, friendly service and a relaxed setting.

filet_du_pecheur.title: Le Filet du Pêcheur
filet_du_pecheur.desc: Classic spot for grilled fish and mixed seafood platters along the coastal road.

ilot_chatain.title: L'îlot Châtain

calypso_medina.title: Calypso Medina
calypso_medina.desc: Lively stop near the corniche for seafood bites, sweet treats and sea-breeze breaks.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Airport transfers and camp shuttles cover most needs. Agree taxi prices before longer citadel or desert tracks.

bargain.title: Wind & sun
bargain.desc: In the potters' quarter, watch the artisans at work. Bargaining is common for craft pieces.

water.title: Cash & bookings
water.desc: Carry dirhams for taxis and small stops. Book accommodation ahead in peak season.

cap_beddouza.title: Cap Beddouza
cap_beddouza.desc: Cliffs and Atlantic panoramas about 25 km away.

essaouira.title: Essaouira
essaouira.desc: UNESCO medina and port, about 2 hours by road.

marrakech.title: Marrakech
marrakech.desc: Leave or return via the ochre city (about 2h30).

q1.question: How many days in Safi?
q1.answer: One day covers the castle, medina and potters. Two to three days add the museum, Kechla and a beach or Cap Beddouza.

q2.question: Is Safi interesting beyond pottery?
q2.answer: Yes: Portuguese sea castle, medina, fishing port and Atlantic coast form a complete heritage and maritime ensemble.

q3.question: How do I get to Safi?
q3.answer: Bus from Casablanca, Marrakech or El Jadida. Nearest airports: Marrakech (RAK) or Casablanca (CMN), then road transfer.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: April to June and September–October offer a good balance. Summer suits the beach but can be windy.
